test.title: Waves and Sound - Test 3
test.description: Previous Year Questions as Chapter Test
test.syllabus: This test contains questions from all topics of this chapter included in the JEE Main syllabus. It includes a mix of questions from PYQs of JEE Main 2019 - 2025.

question.text: Two open organ pipes of lengths $60 \mathrm{~cm}$ and $90 \mathrm{~cm}$ resonate at $6^{\text {th }}$ and $5^{\text {th }}$ harmonics respectively. The difference of frequencies for the given modes is _______ $\mathrm{Hz}$. (Velocity of sound in air $=333 \mathrm{~m} / \mathrm{s}$ )

The equation of wave is given by <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mi>Y</mi><mo>=</mo><msup><mn>10</mn><mrow><mo>-</mo><mn>2</mn></mrow></msup><mi>sin</mi><mn>2</mn><mi>π</mi><mfenced><mrow><mn>160</mn><mi>t</mi><mo>-</mo><mn>0</mn><mo>.</mo><mn>5</mn><mi>x</mi><mo>+</mo><mfrac><mi>π</mi><mn>4</mn></mfrac></mrow></mfenced></math>, where <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mi>x</mi></math> and <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mi>Y</mi></math> are in <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mi>m</mi></math> and <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mi>t</mi></math> in <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mi>s</mi></math>. The speed of the wave is _______ <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mi>km</mi><mo> </mo><msup><mi mathvariant="normal">h</mi><mrow><mo>-</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow></msup></math>.

Two travelling waves of equal amplitudes and equal frequencies move in opposite directions along a string. They interfere to produce a stationary wave whose equation is given by <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mi>y</mi><mo>=</mo><mfenced><mrow><mn>10</mn><mi>cos</mi><mi>π</mi><mi>x</mi><mi>sin</mi><mfrac><mrow><mn>2</mn><mi>π</mi><mi mathvariant="normal">t</mi></mrow><mi mathvariant="normal">T</mi></mfrac></mrow></mfenced><mi>cm</mi></math>. The amplitude of the particle at <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mi>x</mi><mo>=</mo><mfrac><mn>4</mn><mn>3</mn></mfrac><mo> </mo><mi>cm</mi></math> will be _____ <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mi>cm</mi><mo>.</mo></math>

Two waves are simultaneously passing through a string and their equations are : <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><msub><mi>y</mi><mn>1</mn></msub><mo>=</mo><msub><mi>A</mi><mn>1</mn></msub><mi>sin</mi><mi>k</mi><mo>(</mo><mi>x</mi><mo>-</mo><mi>v</mi><mi>t</mi><mo>)</mo><mo>,</mo><msub><mi>y</mi><mn>2</mn></msub><mo>=</mo><msub><mi>A</mi><mn>2</mn></msub><mi>sin</mi><mi>k</mi><mfenced><mrow><mi>x</mi><mo>-</mo><mi>v</mi><mi>t</mi><mo>+</mo><msub><mi>x</mi><mn>0</mn></msub></mrow></mfenced><mo>.</mo></math> Given amplitudes <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><msub><mi>A</mi><mn>1</mn></msub><mo>=</mo><mn>12</mn><mo> </mo><mi>mm</mi></math> and <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><msub><mi>A</mi><mn>2</mn></msub><mo>=</mo><mn>5</mn><mo> </mo><mi>mm</mi></math>,  <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><msub><mi>x</mi><mn>0</mn></msub><mo>=</mo><mn>3</mn><mo>.</mo><mn>5</mn><mo> </mo><mi>cm</mi></math> and wave number <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mi mathvariant="normal">k</mi><mo>=</mo><mn>6</mn><mo>.</mo><mn>28</mn><msup><mrow><mo> </mo><mi>cm</mi></mrow><mrow><mo>-</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow></msup><mo>.</mo></math> The amplitude of resulting wave will be _____ <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mi>mm</mi><mo>.</mo></math>

A tuning fork resonates with a sonometer wire of length <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mn>1</mn><mo> </mo><mi mathvariant="normal">m</mi></math> stretched with a tension of <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mn>6</mn><mo> </mo><mi mathvariant="normal">N</mi><mo>.</mo></math> When the tension in the wire is changed to <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mn>54</mn><mo> </mo><mi mathvariant="normal">N</mi><mo>,</mo></math> the same tuning fork produces <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mn>12</mn></math> beats per second with it. The frequency of the tuning fork is _______ <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mi>Hz</mi><mo>.</mo></math>

The fundamental frequency of vibration of a string between two rigid support is <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mn>50</mn><mo> </mo><mi>Hz</mi></math>. The mass of the string is <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mn>18</mn><mo> </mo><mi mathvariant="normal">g</mi></math> and its linear mass density is <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mn>20</mn><mo> </mo><mi mathvariant="normal">g</mi><mo> </mo><msup><mi mathvariant="normal">m</mi><mrow><mo>-</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow></msup></math>. The speed of the transverse waves so produced in the string is _______ <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mi mathvariant="normal">m</mi><mo> </mo><msup><mi mathvariant="normal">s</mi><mrow><mo>–</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow></msup></math>.

Two travelling waves produces a standing wave represented by equation. <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mi>y</mi><mo>=</mo><mfenced><mrow><mn>1</mn><mo>.</mo><mn>0</mn><mo> </mo><mi>mm</mi></mrow></mfenced><mi>cos</mi><mfenced close="]" open="["><mrow><mfenced><mrow><mn>1</mn><mo>.</mo><mn>57</mn><msup><mrow><mo> </mo><mi>cm</mi></mrow><mrow><mo>-</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow></msup></mrow></mfenced><mi>x</mi></mrow></mfenced><mo> </mo><mi>sin</mi><mfenced close="]" open="["><mrow><mfenced><mrow><mn>78</mn><mo>.</mo><mn>5</mn><msup><mrow><mo> </mo><mi mathvariant="normal">s</mi></mrow><mrow><mo>-</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow></msup></mrow></mfenced><mo> </mo><mi mathvariant="normal">t</mi></mrow></mfenced></math>. The node closest to the origin in the region <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mi>x</mi><mo>></mo><mn>0</mn></math> will be at <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mi>x</mi><mo>=</mo><mo>.</mo><mo>.</mo><mo>.</mo><mo>.</mo><mo>.</mo><mo>.</mo><mo> </mo><mfenced><mrow><mtext>in</mtext><mo> </mo><mi>cm</mi></mrow></mfenced><mo>.</mo></math>

In an experiment to determine the velocity of sound in air at room temperature using a resonance tube, the first resonance is observed when the air column has a length of <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mn>20</mn><mo>.</mo><mn>0</mn><mo> </mo><mi>cm</mi></math> for a tuning fork of frequency <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mn>400</mn><mo> </mo><mi>Hz</mi></math> is used. The velocity of the sound at room temperature is <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mn>336</mn><msup><mrow><mo> </mo><mi mathvariant="normal">m</mi><mo> </mo><mi mathvariant="normal">s</mi></mrow><mrow><mo>-</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow></msup></math>. The third resonance is observed when the air column has a length of _____ <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mi>cm</mi></math>

The distance between two consecutive points with phase difference of <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mn>60</mn><mo>°</mo></math> in a wave of frequency <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mn>500</mn><mo> </mo><mi>Hz</mi></math> is <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mn>6</mn><mo>.</mo><mn>0</mn><mo> </mo><mi mathvariant="normal">m</mi></math>. The velocity with which wave is travelling is ______ <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mi>km</mi><mo> </mo><msup><mi mathvariant="normal">s</mi><mrow><mo>-</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow></msup></math>.

A wire having a linear mass density <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mn>9</mn><mo>.</mo><mn>0</mn><mo>×</mo><msup><mn>10</mn><mrow><mo>-</mo><mn>4</mn></mrow></msup><mo> </mo><mi>kg</mi><mo> </mo><msup><mi mathvariant="normal">m</mi><mrow><mo>-</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow></msup></math> is stretched between two rigid supports with a tension of <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mn>900</mn><mo> </mo><mi mathvariant="normal">N</mi><mo>.</mo></math> The wire resonates at a frequency of <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mn>500</mn><mo> </mo><mi>Hz</mi><mo>.</mo></math> The next higher frequency at which the same wire resonates is <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mn>550</mn><mo> </mo><mi>Hz</mi><mo>.</mo></math> The length of the wire is ___________ <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mi mathvariant="normal">m</mi><mo>.</mo></math>

The amplitude of wave disturbance propagating in the positive <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mi>x</mi></math>-direction is given by <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mi>y</mi><mo>=</mo><mfrac><mn>1</mn><mrow><mo>(</mo><mn>1</mn><mo>+</mo><mi>x</mi><msup><mo>)</mo><mn>2</mn></msup></mrow></mfrac></math> at time <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mi>t</mi><mo>=</mo><mn>0</mn></math> and <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mi>y</mi><mo>=</mo><mfrac><mn>1</mn><mrow><mn>1</mn><mo>+</mo><mo>(</mo><mi>x</mi><mo>-</mo><mn>2</mn><msup><mo>)</mo><mn>2</mn></msup></mrow></mfrac></math> at <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mi>t</mi><mo>=</mo><mn>1</mn><mo> </mo><mi>s</mi></math>, where <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mi>x</mi></math> and <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mi>y</mi></math> are in metres. The shape of wave does not change during the propagation. The velocity of the wave will be <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mi mathvariant="normal">m</mi><mo> </mo><msup><mi mathvariant="normal">s</mi><mrow><mo>-</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow></msup><mo>.</mo></math>
A closed and an open organ pipe have same lengths. If the ratio of frequencies of their seventh overtones is $\left(\frac{a-1}{a}\right)$ then the value of $\mathrm{a}$ is ________

A wire of length <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mn>30</mn><mo> </mo><mi>cm</mi></math>, stretched between rigid supports, has it's <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><msup><mi>n</mi><mrow><mi>th</mi><mo> </mo></mrow></msup></math> and <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><msup><mfenced><mrow><mi>n</mi><mo>+</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow></mfenced><mi>th</mi></msup></math> harmonics at <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mn>400</mn><mo> </mo><mi>Hz</mi></math> and <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mn>450</mn><mo> </mo><mi>Hz</mi></math>, respectively. If tension in the string is <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mn>2700</mn><mo> </mo><mi mathvariant="normal">N</mi></math>, it's linear mass density is _____ <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mi>kg</mi><mo> </mo><msup><mi mathvariant="normal">m</mi><mrow><mo>-</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow></msup></math>.

The speed of a transverse wave passing through a string of length <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mn>50</mn><mo> </mo><mi>cm</mi></math> and mass <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mn>10</mn><mo> </mo><mi mathvariant="normal">g</mi></math> is <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mn>60</mn><mo> </mo><mi mathvariant="normal">m</mi><mo> </mo><msup><mi mathvariant="normal">s</mi><mrow><mo>-</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow></msup></math>. The area of cross-section of the wire is <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mn>2</mn><mo>.</mo><mn>0</mn><mo> </mo><msup><mi>mm</mi><mn>2</mn></msup></math> and its Young's modulus is <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mn>1</mn><mo>.</mo><mn>2</mn><mo>×</mo><msup><mn>10</mn><mn>11</mn></msup><mo> </mo><mi mathvariant="normal">N</mi><mo> </mo><msup><mi mathvariant="normal">m</mi><mrow><mo>-</mo><mn>2</mn></mrow></msup></math>. The extension of the wire over its natural length due to its tension will be <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mi mathvariant="normal">x</mi><mo>×</mo><msup><mn>10</mn><mrow><mo>-</mo><mn>5</mn></mrow></msup><mo> </mo><mi mathvariant="normal">m</mi></math>. The value of <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mi>x</mi></math> is _____ .

A guitar string of length <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mn>90</mn><mo> </mo><mi>cm</mi></math> vibrates with a fundamental frequency of <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mn>120</mn><mo> </mo><mi>Hz</mi></math>. The length of the string producing a fundamental of <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mn>180</mn><mo> </mo><mi>Hz</mi></math> will be _____ <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mi>cm</mi></math>

In a closed organ pipe, the frequency of fundamental note is <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mn>30</mn><mo> </mo><mi>Hz</mi></math>. A certain amount of water is now poured in the organ pipe so that the fundamental frequency is increased to <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mn>110</mn><mo> </mo><mi>Hz</mi></math>. If the organ pipe has a cross-sectional area of <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mn>2</mn><mo> </mo><msup><mi>cm</mi><mn>2</mn></msup></math>, the amount of water poured in the organ tube is ________<math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mi mathvariant="normal">g</mi></math>. (Take speed of sound in air is <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mn>330</mn><mo> </mo><mi mathvariant="normal">m</mi><mo> </mo><msup><mi mathvariant="normal">s</mi><mrow><mo>-</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow></msup></math> )

For a certain organ pipe, the first three resonance frequencies are in the ratio of 1:3:5 respectively. If the frequency of fifth harmonic is 405 Hz and the speed of sound in air is 324 m s–1 the length of the organ pipe is _____ m.

In an experiment with sonometer when a mass of <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mn>180</mn><mo> </mo><mi mathvariant="normal">g</mi></math> is attached to the string, it vibrates with fundamental frequency of <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mn>30</mn><mo> </mo><mi>Hz</mi></math>. When a mass <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mi>m</mi></math> is attached, the string vibrates with fundamental frequency of <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mn>50</mn><mo> </mo><mi>Hz</mi></math>. The value of <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mi>m</mi></math> is ______ <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mi mathvariant="normal">g</mi></math>.

A tuning fork is vibrating at <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mn>250</mn><mo> </mo><mi>Hz</mi></math>. The length of the shortest closed organ pipe that will resonate with the tuning fork will be _____<math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mi>cm</mi></math>. (Take speed of sound in air as <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mn>340</mn><msup><mrow><mo> </mo><mi mathvariant="normal">m</mi><mo> </mo><mi mathvariant="normal">s</mi></mrow><mrow><mo>-</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow></msup></math> )

A wire of density <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mn>8</mn><mo>×</mo><msup><mn>10</mn><mn>3</mn></msup><mo> </mo><mi>kg</mi><mo> </mo><msup><mi mathvariant="normal">m</mi><mrow><mo>-</mo><mn>3</mn></mrow></msup></math> is stretched between two clamps <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mn>0</mn><mo>.</mo><mn>5</mn><mo> </mo><mi mathvariant="normal">m</mi></math> apart. The extension developed in the wire is <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mn>3</mn><mo>.</mo><mn>2</mn><mo>×</mo><msup><mn>10</mn><mrow><mo>-</mo><mn>4</mn></mrow></msup><mo> </mo><mi mathvariant="normal">m</mi></math>. If <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mi>Y</mi><mo>=</mo><mn>8</mn><mo>×</mo><msup><mn>10</mn><mn>10</mn></msup><mo> </mo><mi mathvariant="normal">N</mi><mo> </mo><msup><mi mathvariant="normal">m</mi><mrow><mo>-</mo><mn>2</mn></mrow></msup></math>, the fundamental frequency of vibration in the wire will be _____ <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mi>Hz</mi></math>
